newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rates steady despite drain.
newsitem.headline: German call money rates steady despite drain.

text.p: German call money rates were steady around 3.05 percent on Wednesday despite a smaller than expected allocation in the Bundesbank's market operation.
Some traders said, however, that rates could tick up later as banks looked for funds, although any gains would be limited. "We should continue to go up on average," one trader said.
The Bundesbank drained 1.9 billion marks from the banking system earlier, allocating 84 billion marks in repos at the same time that 85.9 billion marks of repos was expiring.
Traders had expected a relatively neutral allocation.
Banks held 40 billion marks with the Bundesbank on Tuesday compared with 41.5 billion marks the on Monday. The average for the month so far stood at 40.6 billion marks.
Banks borrowed around 100 million marks from the Bundesbank's emergency Lombard lending facility.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average (FIONA) stood at 3.08533 percent on Wednesday compared with 3.07533 percent the day before.
